transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-05-14 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Lena Morris (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Oliver Chen (Redwood CSM), Maya Rivers (Apex Head of Security), Diego Alvarez (Apex SRE Lead), Priya Kumar (Apex Compliance), Ethan Cole (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick security and resilience readout focused on BCDR (RTO/RPO), SSO/KMS integration questions, audit logging, and the escalation process for high-severity incidents. Apex requested clarifications about Redwood's key management and the steps during an outage to meet their 3-hour RTO for critical services. Action items agreed at end.

Topics covered:
- SOC 2 / ISO attestations and evidence handling
- RBAC and SSO (SAML/SCIM) provisioning patterns
- Audit logs, retention, and tamper-resistance
- KMS/HSM options, key rotation, and Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) model
- Incident response workflows, BCDR tabletop cadence, RTO/RPO alignment
- SLA uptime and escalation ladder for Sev 1/Sev 2

Action items (captured in doc header as well)

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we've got about 50 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Maya: Maya here, head of sec at Apex.
[00:15] Diego: Diego, SRE lead.
[00:17] Priya: Priya, compliance.
[00:19] Ethan: Ethan, procurement.
[00:21] Samir: Samir Patel from Redwood SE, hi all.
[00:24] Oliver: Oliver Chen, CSM.
[00:26] Lena: Cool. So agenda: start with attestations, then SSO/KMS, and then deep dive on incident/escalation and RTO/RPO.
[00:36] Maya: Yep, that's perfect. To kick off, are your SOC 2 artifacts current? We need Type II evidence for our audit window Q3.
[00:43] Samir: Yeah, we have a SOC 2 Type II that covers controls for 2025-2026; I've got the bundle but need to scrub a few PII touches before we give you the full pack. I'll upload a sanitized bundle to the secure share, expecting by Monday.
[00:58] Priya: When you say "sanitized" — does that mean redacted logs? We have to show the raw control evidence for our auditor, redaction sometimes is flagged.
[01:06] Samir: Right, good call. We typically provide an auditor-only folder via S3 with restricted access and an NDA. The redaction was more for marketing copies. For auditor access we can provide full artifacts with an access window and IP allowlist.
[01:20] Maya: OK that's acceptable. Also ISO cert?
[01:23] Samir: We have ISO 27001 attestation — I'd send the cert and scope doc.
[01:28] Diego: Great. Now on to SSO, RBAC and provisioning — we want SCIM for user sync, and just-in-time provisioning. How does Redwood support role mapping for multiple teams?
[01:40] Samir: We support SAML 2.0 and SCIM 2.0; role mapping is policy-based in the console. You can map SAML groups to Redwood roles and then enforce fine-grained RBAC. One thing to note, the initial provisioning is a best-effort sync so we recommend a daily reconcile job on your side for our sidecar groups.
[01:58] Maya: Any gotchas with multiple identity providers? We have Okta for corporate and Azure AD for contractors.
[02:05] Samir: Yep, you can configure multiple IdPs — there is a primary IdP for console login and an auxiliary for service principals. There's a small UX caveat where the SCIM token belongs to a single org, so if you use two distinct Azure tenants you'll need separate org mappings. We'll share the SCIM guide.
[02:25] Priya: Please add the SCIM SCOPES doc to the share.
[02:28] Oliver: Note: I will attach the SCIM and SAML integration runbook in the follow-ups.
[02:33] Diego: Cool. Now KMS — we have a BYOK requirement for customer key ownership on certain PII workloads. How do you handle KMS integration and HSM-backed keys?
[02:44] Samir: We offer three patterns: Redwood-managed keys (default), BYOK via customer KMS (Cloud KMS: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) with envelope encryption, and an HSM-backed model for Dedicated/Private deployments. For BYOK, Redwood never stores the plaintext key; we only get wrapped keys via a wrap/unwrap flow.
[03:04] Maya: And key rotation? We need a monthly rotation policy with immutable audit trail.
[03:09] Samir: Rotation is automated on the Redwood side if you use our managed keys. For BYOK you'll control rotation in your KMS. We provide rotation metadata and logs that show when we requested unwraps and which key version was used.
[03:21] Diego: Is that metadata stored in plaintext logs? We need tamper resistance.
[03:26] Samir: The metadata is stored in append-only audit logs with checksuming, and we can stream those logs to your SIEM by syslog or to an S3 bucket. We also support push of logs to your Splunk/Datadog via forwarder.
[03:39] Priya: Retention windows — we require seven years of audit trail for certain regions — is that possible?
[03:46] Samir: On the hosted tier long retention is an add-on; for Dedicated or Private you can set retention to meet regulatory needs. We'll put retention SLAs in the doc.
[03:57] Maya: OK. Next, incident response and Business Continuity / Disaster Recovery. Our target for critical call paths is RTO 3 hours and RPO 15 minutes. Can you meet that for dedicated service?
[04:12] Lena: I can take the SLA pieces, but Samir will walk through the technical enablers.
[04:16] Samir: For Dedicated we typically guarantee a 99.95% uptime SLA, and we have multi-az failover for KV caches and model serving. For RPO 15 minutes that's aggressive for some model-stateful workloads, but with prefix cache replication and cross AZ replication we can get to sub-5 minute RPO for stateless tokens and about 15 minutes for persistent KV caches depending on your workload. For hosted, RTOs are measured differently because of shared infra.
[04:44] Diego: Could you outline the failover steps? If a region goes down, what happens to live sessions / websocket streams?
[04:51] Samir: High level: (1) detect via healthchecks and synthetic probes, (2) route new requests to warm standby region, (3) KV cache replication triggers reconstruction of session context from prefix cache in standby, and (4) model-serving fallback to a compatible variant if your pinned model isn't available. For websockets, we recommend application-layer reconnect with sticky tokens — we provide a reconnect token TTL. There will be a small degradation window for in-progress streaming responses.
[05:20] Maya: Who triggers the escalation? Our internal policy is that if we don't have a mitigation within 30 minutes we go to an executive incident call.
[05:28] Samir: Our on-call SRE is paged automatically for Sev1s. Redwood's internal runbook for Sev1 includes a 15-minute ack target, and we escalate to the SRE lead and then to on-call for the platform manager at 45 minutes if not resolved. We can integrate with your PagerDuty or Opsgenie for joint incident calls.
[05:45] Diego: What counts as Sev1 versus Sev2 for Redwood? Sometimes definitions differ.
[05:50] Samir: Sev1: production outage impacting >30% of requests or failure of critical path; Sev2: degraded performance impacting <30% or partial outages. We'll share the definitive severity matrix in the SLA appendix.
[06:03] Priya: Audit trails for incidents — we need tamper-proof timelines for audits.
[06:08] Samir: Incident timelines are generated from immutable event logs; we also bundle incident notes and the channel history (redacted as needed) into the postmortem. We can provide signed incident artifacts for compliance.
[06:19] Maya: For the exec escalation, can you support an Apex point of contact with direct dial? We need an escalation ladder that matches our internal cadence.
[06:28] Lena: Yes, the escalation ladder we'll send will include 24/7 on-call, phone numbers, and an executive contact for prioritized accounts (that's in the Dedicated contract appendix).
[06:36] Ethan: On procurement side, can you add a liability cap exception for data residency incidents? That's something our legal team will ask.
[06:44] Lena: We'll flag that for legal discussion — not something we can finalize in this call but we'll include the standard enterprise exceptions and iterate.
[06:51] Diego: A hypothetical scenario — primary region fails, we need failover; how is DNS handled and typical TTL expectations?
[07:00] Samir: We recommend a low TTL for DNS records (60s) for hot failover; however, some customers prefer weighted routing to reduce flapping. We provide DNS failover playbooks. In practice, DNS TTL and client caching are the long pole.
[07:14] Maya: For on-prem private deployment — if we go behind our VPC, how is the escalation arranged?
[07:21] Oliver: For Private deployments we provide a customer-facing runbook and a dedicated TAM. The private control plane still allows Redwood to be paged for critical infra problems depending on the support attachment. We'll document the connectivity and the escalation handoff.
[07:36] Maya: Good. A few more specifics on KMS and BYOK: do you support HSM attestation and FIPS-140 compliance?
[07:44] Samir: Our HSM options on Dedicated can be FIPS 140-2 or 140-3 compliant depending on the vendor (we've worked with Thales and AWS CloudHSM). We can provide attestation reports on request.
[07:58] Priya: For data residency — some of our call metadata must remain in the EU. How do you partition logs/metadata?
[08:06] Samir: We can regionally isolate logs and metrics; metadata that includes call traces can be pinned to a geographic region in the Dedicated or Private model. Hosted customers can request regioning but it's an advanced configuration.
[08:20] Diego: Are there limits to streaming history retention if we need long-term retention for compliance?
[08:25] Samir: Historical stream transcripts are subject to retention policies; for long-term retention we suggest exporting to your S3 bucket. We also support export hooks for our audit log stream.
[08:36] Maya: OK, talk me through the tabletop / runbook cadence you recommend.
[08:41] Samir: We suggest quarterly tabletop exercises for critical services and a full BCDR test annually. For high-compliance customers a semi-annual tabletop is common. The sequence: prep -> scenario kickoff -> runbook execution -> postmortem and action items. We can run a dry-run next week.
[09:00] Diego: We'll take you up on that. Who from Redwood runs the tabletop?
[09:04] Oliver: Our SRE and CSM will co-facilitate. Samir will lead the technical parts.
[09:10] Maya: About telemetry — we want to pull raw metrics into our Grafana; do you support Prometheus-compatible endpoints?
[09:18] Samir: Yes, for Dedicated we expose Prometheus endpoints and metric pushes; hosted customers get a metrics stream via exporter.
[09:25] Priya: Any privacy concerns with sending traces to our Grafana? We need to ensure PII is redacted prior to export.
[09:33] Samir: We can configure filters to redact PII in traces prior to export. We'll include guidance on our data classification and filter rules.
[09:41] Diego: One more technical question — KV cache replication lag under load. You've mentioned 15 minute RPO for certain workloads, but what's the real world SLA under 80% CPU?
[09:51] Samir: In our benchmarks under 80% utilization we saw median replication lag at ~60 seconds and tail at ~6 minutes for heavy write workloads. We'll attach the benchmark spreadsheet (link) but note that model architecture and sequence lengths change behavior.
[10:08] Maya: Could you share the benchmark sheet now?
[10:11] Samir: I'll push the sheet after the call — expect it in the share.
[10:15] Ethan: Procurement — we need a clause for scheduled maintenance windows and notification times. What's standard?
[10:21] Lena: Standard maintenance notifications are 48 hours for non-critical updates and an emergency maintenance clause for security patches with as much notice as possible. For Dedicated customers we can coordinate maintenance windows.
[10:33] Priya: Are maintenance windows counted against SLA?
[10:36] Lena: Planned maintenance is excluded from SLA calculations if notified within contract terms; unplanned outages are counted. We'll highlight that in the SLA doc.
[10:44] Maya: Let's walk through a short incident example — say a model binary gets corrupted during deployment causing continuous 500s for a route. What's the immediate mitigation?
[10:54] Samir: Immediate mitigation is to rollback to the last stable model version via our rollout controller, and then fail traffic to a warm variant. If rollback fails, route to a lower-capacity but compatible model. Our rollout controller has automatic canary and instant rollback hooks.
[11:10] Diego: Are rollbacks audited? We need the who/when reason steps captured.
[11:14] Samir: Yes, every rollout/change is logged with the actor, timestamp, diff and can be exported to your audit store.
[11:21] Maya: Good. Any questions from Redwood side?
[11:24] Samir: Nothing more right now.
[11:27] Lena: OK we'll recap. Next steps: Samir to upload SOC2 and benchmarks; Oliver to send KMS note and SCIM runbook; Lena to send SLA/quote; Apex to provide RTO/RPO critical app list. We'll schedule a tabletop on 2026-05-20 pending availabilities.
[11:49] Maya: That works. Anything else on escalation contacts?
[11:53] Oliver: We'll put a named escalation ladder in the appendix.
[11:56] Ethan: Procurement will follow up by email for contract markups.
[11:59] Lena: Great — thanks everyone, we'll send notes and links.
[12:03] Priya: Thanks.

References / Links mentioned:

Call end.
